To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the network performance is mainly affected by the migration rate (i.e., the rate of virtual machines moving from one site to another) rather than by the number of sites involved in the federation.
the network capacity of a cloud federation should be dimensioned in order to satisfy a certain number of virtual machines live migration per unit of time.

the inter-data center link capacity should be dimensioned according to the number of live migration operations, the number of virtual machines involved in each operation, the average size of the virtual machines, the average number of virtual machines that need to migrate at the same time, the average number and the average duration of the live migration operations, and the average number of live migration failures.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (i) how much capacity is required to achieve a certain performance level in terms of migration success rate, and (ii) how to allocate the capacity among the different links of the inter-data centers network.
the following questions: (i) how much capacity is required to guarantee a given performance in terms of migration time?
a quantitative assessment of the performance of a cloud federation, which is a key step towards its effective design and management.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach can be a valuable tool for cloud federation providers in order to design and dimension the network infrastructure in an efficient way.

, in a cloud federation, a careful dimensioning of the inter-data-center network capacity, based on a proper characterization of virtual machine live migration performance, can be the key to guarantee a high degree of user satisfaction.
, in order to obtain a good network performance, the network bandwidth should be increased as the number of data centers and the amount of migrated virtual machines increases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in a cloud federation scenario, a network capacity dimensioning approach based on a simple virtual machine live migration strategy can provide a good tradeoff between the network capacity cost and the user’s quality of experience.

the proposed analytical model is able to provide an effective tool for network designers, in order to dimension the network infrastructure in cloud federations, in a cost-effective way, while ensuring the desired quality of service for the virtual machine migration process.

, by means of the proposed model, it is possible to estimate the required bandwidth to support multiple virtual machine live migrations across data centers, with a given level of network performance, in order to guarantee a given level of quality of service to the end user.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the performance of the cloud federation network is strongly dependent on the virtual machine placement strategy, the number of data centers, and the number of virtual machines to be moved at the same time.

the inter-data center bandwidth should not be dimensioned only according to the average number of concurrent virtual machines being migrated, but also according to its peak values, as well as to the number of concurrent migrations that are allowed to be performed at a time, in order to avoid the network congestion and guarantee the required performance levels.
a careful dimensioning of the inter-data centers network is essential to guarantee the performance of multiple live migration strategies.
